title: Why purple, and not red
excerpt: For twenty-five years I corrected notebooks in purple ink. Here is why — and why it became Nemara's colour.
author: Pratima Saxena

body.text: In my first year of teaching, a girl in the third row cried when she saw her notebook. It wasn't the marks. It was the red. Every line I had underlined looked like a wound.
The next morning I bought a purple pen. I used it for the next twenty-five years.
Red is a correction. Purple is a conversation.

When I began drawing jewellery, the sketches were in the same ink — because that was the pen in my bag. Somewhere along the way, the colour stopped being a tool and became a point of view. Nemara is that point of view: you are not being corrected. You are being noticed.

title: Four hundred coils: making the Raat Rani collar
excerpt: Inside Ramesh Soni's Cuttack workshop, where one necklace takes eleven days and a great deal of patience.
author: Nemara Studio

cover.alt: Placeholder — Raat Rani sketch on the design table

body.text: Ramesh starts each petal with a frame of silver no thicker than a pencil line. He fills it with coils — twisted, flattened, curled — until the frame looks like lace.
There are twenty-one petals. Each has its own small differences, because each was made on a different morning, in different light.
The lace is what holds the shape. — Ramesh Soni
Once linked, the collar is plated in gold vermeil and the violet stones are set one at a time. It is, in Ramesh's words, 'a slow necklace for fast evenings'.

title: One kada, five versions of you
excerpt: The Ink & Gold pair, worn from a Monday stand-up to a Saturday sangeet.
author: Nemara Studio

cover.alt: Placeholder — kadas stacked on the wrist

body.text: Monday: one kada, crisp white shirt, sleeves pushed up. The purple line does the talking.
Wednesday: both kadas with a watch on the other wrist. Balanced, not matched.
Friday: stack them with the Recess bracelet. Play is allowed.
Saturday: with a silk saree and the Monsoon Hour jhumkas — gold to gold, lilac to purple.
Sunday: give one to your sister. She'll know why.
